# Berlin Deposit Dispute: Tenant-Friendly Documentation Plan

A landlord in Germany generally needs a clear reason to withhold a deposit, and minor wear is often treated differently from actual damage. Based on your description, the safest move is to document everything carefully and ask for a written breakdown before agreeing to any deduction.

## What to Document Before You Reply

- **Move-out condition photos/videos** from every room, including:
  - wall scuffs
  - the broken cabinet hinge
  - floors, windows, appliances, bathroom fixtures
- **Date-stamped evidence** if available:
  - move-out photos
  - move-out checklist
  - handover protocol / Übergabeprotokoll
- **Proof of normal use vs. damage**
  - note whether the wall marks were minor scuffs or holes
  - note whether the cabinet hinge was old/worn or newly broken
- **Communications**
  - emails, texts, WhatsApp messages with the landlord or agent
  - any prior notice about repairs or complaints
- **Financial records**
  - lease agreement
  - deposit amount and payment proof
  - final utility statements if relevant
- **Witnesses**
  - anyone who saw the apartment at handover or before move-out

## What to Ask For in Writing

- **Exact reason for withholding the deposit**
- **Itemized deduction list** with amounts for each claimed issue
- **Photos or repair invoices** supporting each deduction
- **Confirmation of the deposit balance** they intend to return
- **Timeline for return** of the undisputed amount
- **Whether they are claiming repair costs, cleaning costs, or both**
- **A copy of the signed handover protocol** if one exists

## Tenant-Friendly Checklist

| Item | What to Gather | Why It Helps |
|---|---|---|
| Move-out photos | Clear, date-stamped images of each room | Shows the apartment condition on departure |
| Damage details | Close-ups of scuffs and hinge issue | Helps distinguish minor wear from real damage |
| Handover record | Signed Übergabeprotokoll, if any | Strong evidence of what was noted at handover |
| Messages | Emails, texts, WhatsApp threads | Shows what was discussed and when |
| Lease + deposit proof | Contract and bank transfer proof | Confirms deposit amount and tenancy dates |
| Repair claims | Invoices, estimates, or contractor notes | Lets you challenge unsupported deductions |

## Polite Message Template to Request the Deposit Back

**Subject:** Request for return of security deposit

Hello [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I hope you are well. I am writing regarding the security deposit for the apartment at [address], which I moved out of on 2026-03-31.

I understand you may have concerns about the condition of the apartment. From my side, the apartment had only minor wall scuffs and one broken cabinet hinge, with no major damage. I would appreciate it if you could please send me:

- a written explanation for any amount you intend to withhold
- an itemized list of deductions
- any supporting photos, invoices, or repair estimates
- the amount and timeline for returning the remaining deposit

Please return the undisputed part of the deposit as soon as possible, and let me know in writing if you believe any deduction is necessary.

Thank you for your time and I look forward to your reply.

Kind regards,
[Your full name]
[Your phone number]
[Your email address]

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Save evidence] https://www.google.com/search?q=Germany+tenant+move-out+checklist+deposit+photos
